sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Cutoff 20 October 2026. Accretion Nutraveda Limited, BSE SME 544694, ISIN INE1KVQ01019, is distinct from Accretion Pharmaceuticals. The June filing explicitly says NSE not listed. Listing was 4 February 2026; 7.24 million shares and a 1,000-share lot are corroborated. Accounts are standalone Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, not Ind AS; no subsidiary/group consolidation is substituted. The input CSV is undated and unverified. The latest audited financial balance sheet read is March 2026. HDFC SKY shows ₹295 on its index-constituent page dated 19 October, but this is a delayed secondary snapshot, not an authenticated BSE closing trade. Overall evidence confidence is Medium for business quality and Low for implementation. G1/G2 hold for reporting reconciliation, G3 conditional funding, G4 unresolved. [N26, NSH, NSEC, NPRICE]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors: GOV4, MOAT3, REV8, DUR4, CAP4, CASH2, BAL5, EXEC4, EARN4. REV is capped at8 for the short usable history and Medium comparability, despite a calculated FY2023–FY2026 revenue CAGR of126.21%. No further trajectory bonus. CASH2 reflects repeated material cash absorption rather than one isolated capex year. BQS exact weighted arithmetic is shown below; GQS raw5.40 is capped at5.00 for persistent CASH≤3. D3 is a severe funding-stress assessment, not a predicted default. R and L remain NS: no reweighting or fabricated score. P2 is conditional on the clearly labeled ₹295 secondary snapshot and demanding earnings expectations. Numeric quality scores do not override reporting or implementation holds.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company formulates and manufactures Ayurvedic and nutraceutical products for customer brands across tablets, capsules, oral liquids, powders, oils and external preparations. It is a small contract manufacturer, not a pharmaceutical innovator with proven patent economics. FY2026 product revenue mix was external preparations32.95%, capsules21.35%, tablets15.52%, powders13.57%, oral liquids10.61% and oils6%. Direct exports were only ₹0.1195 crore, down from ₹0.5401 crore, although merchant-export customers can create indirect overseas exposure. Management commentary that both export and domestic growth were strong does not match direct-export revenue. Sanand production and a compact workforce create location/key-person concentration. [N26]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Customer formulation work and manufacturing qualification create some service value, but neither durable pricing power nor patent protection is established. The prospectus acknowledges intense competition and absence of long-term customer agreements. Top-ten customers were85.91% of FY2025 sales and87.67% of H1FY2026 sales; the largest was30.21% and26.01% respectively. Losing one buyer could overwhelm a thinly diversified revenue base. FY2025 utilization ranged from7.15% in oils to82.80% in external preparations; apparent spare aggregate capacity cannot be transferred freely among dosage forms. H1 annualized capsule utilization84.09% supports selective expansion, not a blanket full-capacity shortage. Walpar Nutritions and Influx Healthtech are prospectus comparators, but their IPO-era half-year EPS/price table is not a current comparable valuation set. Certifications are market-access prerequisites, not proof of an economic moat. [NRHP]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Revenue history in ₹crore: FY2022 0.58506; FY2023 2.9031; FY2024 5.0052; FY2025 16.0018; FY2026 33.6031. FY2022 was an early operating year, so the175.29% four-year CAGR greatly overstates mature repeatability. FY2023–FY2026 CAGR is126.21%, also from a tiny base. FY2026 growth was110.0%; no acquisition is disclosed in the reviewed issuer accounts. Volume/utilization and expanded external-preparation capacity support some real scale-up, but a complete price/volume bridge is not disclosed. Working-capital assets grew with sales, and receivables increased faster than sales. As of the cutoff no H1FY2026–27 financial release was located on the issuer financial-results index; no H1 estimate is annualized into reported revenue. [N23, NRHP, N26]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: IPO machinery allocations totaled ₹12.2489 crore; ₹5.95 crore was paid by March, matching capital advances, leaving ₹6.2989 crore scheduled machinery spending. The annual report describes installation initiated, not independently verified commercial commissioning. Cash earmarked to unspent IPO objects is not surplus distributable cash. Incremental capital employed using equity+debt−all cash/deposits rose from ₹8.8952 crore to ₹29.9565 crore. Core EBIT after removing other income rose from ₹3.5020 crore to ₹6.6331 crore. Applying a disclosed historical17.16% tax assumption gives incremental NOPAT/IC12.32%; at25% tax it is11.15%. Against an explicitly assumed12–16% capital hurdle, economic value creation is not established. Using a constant15–18% EBIT margin on incremental revenue produces roughly10.39–12.46% incremental returns at17.16% tax. IPO cash and capitalized preliminary costs distort closing/average ratios; removing costs from the denominator without charging their economic burden would flatter returns. The next milestone is productive commissioning plus collections, not another percentage growth target. [N26, NUSE, NRHP]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Six promoters manage interlinked healthcare entities. June promoter-group ownership was73.48%, with no pledged/NDU/other encumbered promoter shares reported; this is dated evidence, not perpetual assurance. FY2026 director remuneration totaled₹0.5668 crore, with another₹0.0630 crore professional fees. Related-party sales₹0.5718 crore and purchases₹0.8040 crore are disclosed, not automatically abusive. Unmodified financial/IFC opinions are favorable, but audit-trail wording conflicts: the audit says logging operated throughout relevant transactions, while the accounting note says database-layer logging was not enabled. CARO mentions related-party loans renewed and accrued interest added, whereas the borrowing/RPT notes do not reconcile those balances. Prospectus restatements corrected omitted tax/gratuity and subsidy/capital classifications; statutory-form and payment delays were disclosed. These are specific control concerns, not proof of intent. The prospectus separately disclosed promoter/group allegations concerning drug quality and child-labour compliance. The latter matter was transferred for jurisdiction, not acquitted; current outcomes were not verified. The issuer was not described as a named criminal defendant in the prospectus issuer section. No minor-identifying information is reproduced. October9 shareholders approved broad business-object changes, borrowing authorization of₹500 crore in excess of capital/reserves/premium, and₹100 crore loan/guarantee/investment limits. These are permissions, not actual debt or diversion. The notice explicitly preserves IPO object restrictions. [NSH, N26, NRHP, NBAL, NOUT]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: The financial-history tables preserve statutory and prospectus-restated series separately. FY2025 statutory PAT₹2.5009 crore becomes₹2.6128 crore in the RHP after depreciation−0.0199, prior tax timing+0.1010, subsidy+0.0476, deferred tax−0.0164 and gratuity−0.0003. FY2024 statutory0.7233 becomes0.8219; FY2023 statutory0.2008 becomes0.2806. FY2026 comparatives revert to original statutory numbers, so a blended PAT CAGR is misleading. FY2025 CFO is−2.2907 in the original annual,−2.2127 in the RHP and−2.2164 in FY2026 comparatives; most original-to-latest difference is interest/interest-income classification, not new cash. FY2026 operating cash includes preliminary expenses3.9064; IPO issue-cost allocation is3.3287, leaving0.5777 needing classification detail. These may be equity-issuance costs, so do not charge all to recurring EBITDA automatically. A full asset write-off sensitivity lowers book equity to31.5668 crore before any tax effect. Core FY2026 PAT after excluding other income and using17.16–25% tax on core PBT6.0989 is approximately4.5742–5.0523 crore before unresolved cost adjustments. Fully diluted current-share EPS on reported PAT is₹7.0004, not the weighted-average₹9.35. FY2026 CFO less cash capex is−15.4590 crore; adjusting only preliminary-expense classification still gives−11.5526 crore. Receivables8.1117 imply88.1 closing days versus74.5 previously. Inventory8.9949 implies136.2 days on material cost less stock movement; customer ageing columns are poorly labeled, so do not treat all balances as independently confirmed. Debt4.2282 rose despite a narrative of reduction; cash/deposits9.7449 include6.5548 earmarked IPO money. After reserving this and debt, the apparent net cash becomes−1.0381 crore, before other commitments. [N26, N25, NRHP, NUSE]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At the ₹295 secondary historical close dated October 12 (not October 19), 0.724 crore shares imply₹213.58 crore equity value and42.14×reported FY2026 PAT, or42.28–46.69×the bounded core PAT estimate. The weighted-average EPS would incorrectly suggest31.55×. A five-year operating/funding illustration is attached, starting from the verified March balance sheet, not pretending it is October cash. Base growth20/15/12/10/8%, EBIT18%,20% tax,14% interest, machinery cash6.2989 in year1, WC50%incremental revenue, maintenance0.4 and additional growth investment0.4×incremental sales; debt principal0.4467 then0.8 each year. At15×terminal NOPAT,0.5%annual dilution, retained excess cash once and1%entry/exit costs, illustrative terminal price is₹198.59 and return−7.98%. Bull growth needs₹0.8975 crore additional funding to maintain a₹1 crore reserve, so no funded bull IRR is shown. This is not an executable valuation: current project progress, deposits, financing schedule and September cash have not been reconciled. R remains NS rather than promote a stale bridge to Medium confidence. Current peer filings/multiples were not verified, so IPO comparables are not used to justify the exit multiple. [N26, NUSE, NPRICE]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: A severe, explicitly hypothetical path combines loss of a large customer with30%first-year revenue decline,8%EBIT margin initially,45 extra receivable days,10%existing receivable loss,15%inventory loss,₹0.5 crore supplier withdrawal and₹0.5 crore compliance contingency. Remaining machinery commitments continue, discretionary incremental growth capex stops, and no automatic working-capital release is credited. This creates a₹3.1292 crore cash-reserve funding gap. It is not a forecast of default or a quantified legal liability. Equity issuance, expensive refinancing or project delay could impair per-share value; an already demanding earnings multiple provides little protection. Conversely March IPO deposits and modest reported debt provide a real buffer, and a partial collection release could improve survival. D3 reflects the supported severe funding/recapitalization risk, with Medium evidence confidence and High forecast uncertainty. No terminal-return number is valid for an unfunded bear path.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five- and ten-baggers over five years require37.97% and58.49%annual share-price compounding before friction. At₹295 and0.724 crore shares, constant-share equity values would need₹1,067.9 crore and₹2,135.8 crore. Even an assumed25×earnings exit requiresPAT42.716/85.432 crore; at15%net margins this means revenue284.77/569.55 crore, approximately53.3%/76.1%five-year revenue CAGR from FY2026, before dilution. Those paths require much larger capacity, customers and internally funded working capital than demonstrated. A small-base historical CAGR does not prove either outcome. No5×/10× probability is assigned.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Before reconsideration: reconcile IPO-restated versus statutory opening accounts; obtain the breakup and treatment of₹3.9064 crore preliminary expenses; reconcile CARO loan language and audit-trail coverage; obtain latest promoter pledge/shareholding and case-status filings; verify commercial commissioning, machinery balances and post-March IPO utilization; reconcile H1FY2026–27 CFO and current cash restrictions. Quantitative checks: receivable days below75 without factoring/recourse shift, inventory days improving, positive cumulative operating cash after excluding equity-issuance classification, and incremental returns sustainably above an assumed12–16%hurdle. Verify a60-session BSE value-turnover series, zero days, current lot/series/circuit/surveillance and executable spread before sizing. Any funded growth plan must show an annual cash bridge, not just a newly authorized borrowing ceiling. Recovered secondary history has 41 observed rows in the 60-session window. Lower-turnover observed median ₹816750 implies 12.24 sessions at 5% participation; conditional missing-equals-zero median ₹548400 implies 18.23 sessions. At 2%/10%, the latter becomes 45.59/9.12 sessions. Missing rows are not proven zero trades. The one-lot cost is ₹295000; current BSE restrictions/circuit regime and provider completeness remain unverified, so L stays NS rather than treating the proxy as a complete exchange execution test. Latest provider trade is October 12 at ₹295; the prior October 19 snapshot date was not a trade date.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Classification: rapid-growth, low-cash-quality SME on a reporting and implementation hold. Completed fundamental assessment is adverse/conditional, not a buy recommendation. BQS/GQS may be compared only with similarly evidenced quality assessments; no IAS ranking or position sizing is supported. Even at one lot, the reference exposure is₹2.95 lakh; a₹5 lakh position cannot be represented precisely because one/two lots mean₹2.95/5.90 lakh before costs. A lower observed share price alone would not resolve accounting comparability, recoverability, commissioning or exit risk.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary-source hierarchy: issuer annual reports and IPO restatements, filed utilization/shareholding and October ballot outcomes, then official exchange security metadata. Web extraction failed for the large annual PDFs and fresh ballot PDFs; direct downloads from the same verified issuer URLs were read instead. The secondary quote is explicitly separated from exchange evidence. All model growth, margins, working-capital intensity, repayment timing, tax/interest sensitivities, exit multiples and distress shocks are analyst assumptions, not guidance. The framework uses all nine canonical factors and exact weights without renormalizing missing IAS factors. Unresolved evidence is retained in limitations; no blank regulator lookup is interpreted as a clean record.
